claim_verdicts.evidence: Conditioned recommendation, supported by tracking.md: "If the entities retrieved from the database don't need to be updated, then a no-tracking query should be used." and "A tracking query means any changes to entity instances are persisted by SaveChanges."

Docs hedge: tracking.md "They're generally quicker to execute"; for a tracking query that finds an entity already in the context "the same instance is returned, which can potentially use less memory and be faster than a no-tracking query"; efficient-querying: no-tracking "duplicates the same Blog 100 times". The benchmark (380.11 KB -> 232.89 KB, 1,414.7 us -> 993.3 us) supports the usual case, not every endpoint.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: You notice this when an endpoint that returns many entities usually uses less time and memory after adding `AsNoTracking()`, with its SQL unchanged.

issues.quote: You notice this when an endpoint that returns many entities uses less time and memory after adding `AsNoTracking()`, with its SQL unchanged.
issues.text: Unconditional. Docs say no-tracking is 'generally quicker' and that a tracking query can 'potentially use less memory and be faster' (identity resolution; no-tracking duplicates a row referenced many times). Claim 13 rephrased.
issues.fix: Insert 'usually': '...an endpoint that returns many entities usually uses less time and memory after adding `AsNoTracking()`, with its SQL unchanged.' Update claim 13 text to match. Do not explain identity resolution (depth_notes).
